result:
**Rebuttal for 21**

Debater B's case rests on two claims, and both fail.

First, B says only straight cuts are valid. The problem explicitly allows a cut that "only goes down and/or right along grid lines," which is a staircase. Straight cuts are a special case, so ruling out staircases needs an argument, not an assertion.

Second, B's vertical-cut argument is a non sequitur. A vertical cut at w gives pieces of size w×2025 and (2024−w)×2025. These need not be equal to form a rectangle, since pieces can be rotated and reflected, and B never considers that case.

B's gcd(2024, 2025) = 1 point also doesn't work. A staircase needs a shared period only within its own step pattern, not across both dimensions. Coprimality of the side lengths says nothing about whether a single step (a₀, d₀) with a₀ < W and d₀ < H/2 can be realized.

B also concedes that the exclusion of staircases "rests on small-case checks and a periodicity heuristic." That concession undercuts B's claim that "the only verified answer is 1." An unproven exclusion is not a verified count.

The arithmetic is also checkable. The 22 divisors of 2³·3⁴·5²·11·23 in [1012, 2024] split into the four blocks listed above, each enumerated explicitly. Removing 2024 leaves 21. B has no counter-list of divisors, so the 21 candidate dimensions stand.
